deviation: The draft gives the Supplier and its licensors ownership of all IP in the "Services", which could include bespoke deliverables, and it says nothing about Customer ownership of deliverables or a perpetual licence to any supplier tooling. This breaks the playbook rule that Customer must own bespoke deliverables, and it leaves Arcadia without secure rights to use what it paid for.
suggested_text: 8.1 The Customer owns all intellectual property rights in (a) the Customer Data and (b) all deliverables created specifically for the Customer under this Agreement, and the Supplier assigns to the Customer all rights it may have in them on creation. 8.2 The Supplier retains ownership of its pre-existing tools and materials ("Supplier Tools") and grants the Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use the Supplier Tools as incorporated within the deliverables. 8.3 The Customer retains all intellectual property rights in its pre-existing materials. 8.4 The Customer grants the Supplier a limited, non-exclusive licence to use Customer Data solely to provide the Services to the Customer during the term of this Agreement.
